name: agent-bridge-cutover
description: Tier-P F1 cutover-resilience scenario: install + provision agent-bridge on a fresh box, then drive the installer's real `agent-bridge deploy` seam (the OS-agnostic zdd active/passive graceful cutover) through a battery of THORNY situations and assert the binding invariant of the correct-install-flows effort (dotfiles#1393) -- a version cutover must NEVER kill in-flight, non-resumable work. agent-bridge stands a new daemon up beside the old (start --passive on a fresh port), health-gates it, flips the routing table (active.json), drains the old at the TURN boundary, and retires it. Checks: (routing-flip-retire) deploy stands a new daemon up beside the old, flips the routing table, and retires the old, and clients resolve the new daemon (beside-not-in-place; nothing hard-killed); (drain-gate) `drain` opens the gate (/health -> draining -- the turn boundary at which new work is refused and in-flight work is waited on) and `undrain` releases it; (breadcrumb-recover) an aborted cutover that strands a DRAINED survivor is healed by recovery (deploy --recover undrains it). FIDELITY: a fully live 'turn survives the flip' assertion needs a real model/ACP child and is a Tier-E concern; this Tier-P probe proves the cutover MECHANISM the turn-survival guarantee is built on (routing flip + retirement, the drain gate/turn boundary, cooperative recovery). The probe is portable stdlib-only, so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.
